subject: SLO fitment playbook + next steps for Acme AI (p95/p99 targets)
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jane Patel <jane.patel@acme.ai>, Ravi Singh <r.singh@acme.ai>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: SLO fitment playbook + next steps for Acme AI (p95/p99 targets)

Hi Jane / Ravi —

Thanks again for the call earlier where we walked through your inference workload and the performance objectives. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're all aligned: 

Summary of your targets: 
- End-to-end (client → model → client) latency SLOs: p95 <= 220ms, p99 <= 480ms for typical user queries (avg payload ~350 tokens).
- Streaming requirement: clients expect segment streaming for interactive chat; first-token latency < 150ms is an important UX metric for you.
- Peak concurrency: 1,200 concurrent active sessions during business hours; sustained throughput ~4,000 requests/minute; spikes up to 8,000 RPM during batch events.
- Payload shape: median response length ~300–400 tokens; 95th percentile up to 1,200 tokens (we saw in your sample CSV).

What Redwood proposes for evaluation: 
1) Short hosted proof-of-fit (7-day): run your anonymized traffic sample against Redwood hosted endpoints with a small dedicated pool. Goal is to measure E2E p95/p99 and first-token streaming latency.
2) Controlled load tests: SE-driven ramp tests to validate concurrency and throughput at target token lengths.
3) Instrumentation handoff: we need a short-lived read-only S3/CSV export of request shape + timestamps or access to a synthetic harness (preferred) — you mentioned the acme-prod-traffic-sample.csv during the call.

Questions / asks from Acme to proceed: 
- Confirm the exact tokenization scheme used for measuring token counts in your CSV (we want to ensure we match your tokenizer).
- Provide a short list of 3 worst-case prompt templates you care about (long system prompts, multi-turn history, tool calls).
- Decide if you want us to simulate client-side network conditions (we can add 30–60ms RTT to mimic your east-coast users).

Proposed timeline: 
- Today: Redwood sends the formal eval plan and an invite for the kickoff tech check (attached .ics).
- By Thu: Acme shares the tokenization note + 3 prompt templates + traffic sample (you suggested an anonymized CSV).
- Next Mon: Kickoff + first small-scale hosted test (we'll capture p95/p99 and streaming first-token numbers).

I'll attach the mutual action plan draft and a small invite for the tech check. Thanks — look forward to validating this.

Best,
Diego
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: mutual-action-plan.docx, redwood-hosted-eval-invite.ics

From: Jane Patel <jane.patel@acme.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ravi Singh <r.singh@acme.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLO fitment playbook + next steps for Acme AI (p95/p99 targets)

Diego — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers inline: 

- Tokenization: we use the tiktoken-like BPE tokenizer (GPT-compat) and the CSV already reports token counts per request in column "tok_count". We'll label any rows that include PII and remove them before sharing the file.
- Prompt templates: attaching the 3 templates we discussed (long-system, multi-turn-history, tool-call). We'll mark which are high-priority for UX.
- Network conditions: yes please — please add ~45ms RTT in the hosted eval to reflect our east-coast user base.

One note on SLOs: the p99 = 480ms target is tight given our largest responses (~1,200 tokens). If Redwood can demonstrate caching/streaming first-token under 150ms and maintain p95 <= 220ms for 95% of requests, that would be a win; we understand the p99 will include heavy tails and want to see the trade-offs (quantization, batching).

Sending the anonymized CSV via secure S3 link later today. Also copying our SRE alias for any telemetry questions.

Thanks — Jane
Director of Product
Acme AI

Attachments: acme_prompt_templates.txt

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jane Patel <jane.patel@acme.ai>, Ravi Singh <r.singh@acme.ai>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Jul 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLO fitment playbook + next steps for Acme AI (p95/p99 targets)

Hi Jane / Ravi —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the tokenizer detail — that helps a lot. Operational notes from our side and the concrete eval plan: 

Eval plan (technical):
- Phase A (sanity, 24–48h): replay your anonymized CSV at low QPS to baseline p50/p95/p99 and verify token counts align. We will run with your tokenizer settings.
- Phase B (streaming first-token): enable chunked responses for the three template types and measure first-byte/first-token latency for streaming under 50/200/800 concurrent sessions.
- Phase C (stress): controlled ramps to 1,200 concurrency and spikes to 2,500 to validate autoscaling behavior and p99 tails. We'll also run one long-tail test with token lengths up to 1,200.

Measurement plan and instrumentation:
- We'll export per-request timestamps (client-send, server-receive, first-token, last-token) and aggregated p50/p95/p99.
- If you can provide a temporary S3 bucket with CSV or a signed URL, we'll pull it directly. Otherwise, we can provide a secure upload endpoint.

Trade-offs we'll capture:
- Batching size vs first-token latency (we'll show curves at 16/64/128 batch sizes).
- Quantization profile impact on latency and quality (we'll include a short eval of opt-Q4 variants).
- CPU vs GPU fallbacks if dedicated capacity is constrained.

Deliverables after the 7-day hosted run: 
- Raw latency histograms (p50/p90/p95/p99) per template and token length bucket.
- First-token streaming breakdown with 95% CI.
- A short recommendations doc listing config levers (batching, cache TTLs, quant profiles) with estimated cost/latency trade-offs.

Next steps we need from Acme: 
- Signed NDA addendum for the short-term hosted eval (we can send a one-paragraph addendum).
- The anonymized CSV (or upload) and the 3 prompt templates (thanks for sending).
- Availability window for a 30-minute tech check (engineer-only) — options: Mon 10am PT or Tue 11am PT.

I'll schedule the tech check for Monday 10am PT unless you prefer the Tue slot.

—Camila
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: acme-prod-traffic-sample.csv (pending), eval-metrics-schema.yml

From: Ravi Singh <r.singh@acme.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>, Jane Patel <jane.patel@acme.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, acme-sre@acme.ai
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLO fitment playbook + next steps for Acme AI (p95/p99 targets)

Camila — Monday 10am PT works for our engineering lead. We'll upload the anonymized CSV to the S3 link by EOD today and include the token_count column as you requested. NDA addendum is fine — send it over and we'll sign.

Small note on metrics: please include server-side breakdowns (receive queue, model decode time, network egress) — our SRE wants to see where p99 mass is occurring. If you can add a simple trace diagram in the deliverable that maps timestamps to components, that will help our post-eval decision.

Looking forward to the run.

—Ravi
Head of SRE, Acme AI
